1: Above a burning city in Miami of 2051, an ordinary high school biology teacher falls from the sky after being dragged into a war thirty years in the future.
2: He barely survives by plunging into a rooftop pool, only to find the soldiers who fell before him lying dead all around.
3: And in this hellish future, he is about to meet someone he never could have imagined meeting.
4: The story goes back twenty-eight years to December 2022, where Dan, a former soldier who served in Iraq, now teaches high school biology.
5: Dreaming of working at a real research lab, Dan goofs around with his bright daughter Muri and waits for a job offer call while a party for the World Cup final is in full swing at home.
6: While everyone is absorbed in the soccer match, his wife Emmy hands him a Christmas card from his father in the kitchen, and Dan's expression hardens.
7: Having cut off contact with his father for many years, Dan changes the subject at the mere mention of his name.
8: However, the answer that comes back is a rejection due to his lack of civilian experience.
9: Furious, Dan hurls his folder to the floor on yet another night when his dream of becoming a researcher is shattered.
10: Young Muri comes over to sit beside her dejected father, and the two watch the World Cup final side by side.
11: In the middle of the match, however, the center of the stadium flashes and armed soldiers walk out of the smoke, led by a young officer named Lieutenant Hart.
12: After that moment, the world changes completely as armies from every nation leave for the future to fight alien monsters called White Spikes, only for a handful of troops to return seven days later.
13: Ultimately, the world's first global draft begins, and with the survival rate of conscripted civilians falling below twenty percent, anti-war protests spread across the streets.
14: Conscription becomes everyone's worst nightmare, to the point that even young Muri has bad dreams about her mother being taken away.
15: It is the same at school, where students talk back and ask what the point of studying even is.
16: During class, none of the students raise their hands except for Martin, who only talks about volcanoes.
17: Just as Dan is trying to calm the students down, his phone rings with a draft notice.
18: Reporting to the induction center the next day without knowing what is going on, Dan takes off his shirt and is weighed down with all kinds of gear.
19: Because only people who have already died in the future are drafted, Dan is notified that he will die in seven years, though they refuse to tell him how.
20: A jump band is then forcibly embedded into his arm along with a warning that his wife or daughter will be taken in his place if he runs away.
21: His wife Emmy, a therapist who sees returning draftees every day, is all the more terrified because of it.
22: At a support group for returning draftees, a man who lost his leg recalls the sounds of that fateful day.
23: Hoping to get the jump band removed and run away, Dan visits his father James, an anti-government mechanical engineering master who abandoned him as a child.
24: Living alone in an airport hangar, his father immediately starts nagging about his son's beard the moment they meet.
25: His father boasts that he can take the jump band off using his sketchy equipment.
26: However, the conversation between the long-estranged father and son quickly turns sharp.
27: Although his father explains that he left because he could not control his anger after returning from Vietnam, Dan still cannot forgive him in the end.
28: Realizing that running away would mean abandoning his family just like his father did, Dan decides to leave with the band still on and confesses everything to Emmy when he gets home.
29: To his daughter, who is digging in the yard saying she is looking for a vaccine, Dan carefully begins to say his goodbyes.
30: Civilians of all ages and professions gather at the draft center for just a single week of training before a seven-day, 168-hour tour of duty.
31: Standing next to him is a chatty scientist named Charlie, who admits he talks too much whenever he gets nervous.
32: The man in the pink shirt is Dorian, a survivor of the very first jump into Russia who is now on his third tour.
33: The passage to the future is the Jumplink, a structure that works like two rafts on a river of time moving thirty years apart, allowing travel only between those two points.
34: Sitting on his bunk, Charlie talks about his jellyfish shirt and reveals that his beach-loving wife never came back from the first draft.
35: That very night, however, an emergency alarm blares, wiping out their entire remaining week of training.
36: Dan shows Charlie, who has never even held a gun before, how to load his weapon as the countdown begins beneath a massive purple vortex.
37: Because the coordinates are off, however, the soldiers pour out dozens of meters high in the Miami sky, and most of them plummet straight to the ground.
38: Dropping from the sky onto rooftops and streets, those who hit the hard ground never get back up again.
39: The only survivors are the few who landed in the swimming pool, bringing us right back to the very first scene.
40: Looking down through binoculars at a city reduced to smoke and rubble, Nora takes the lead to scout the way.
41: Over the radio, Romeo Command issues orders and warns that the city is about to be wiped out by carpet bombing.
42: Tasked with rescuing a research team before the bombing begins, Dan naturally takes point as a former special forces soldier.
43: As they move through ruined streets filled only with burned cars and fallen soldiers, Dorian mutters a bitter remark.
44: Upon reaching the lab with spikes embedded in its walls, they find bloodied corpses hanging from the ceiling.
45: White spikes are lodged into every wall, and claw marks from something crawling across the floor trail through the room.
46: With the research team wiped out, they have to salvage at least the twelve blue ampoules containing their findings while something unseen watches them from the shadows.
47: As the group heads down the dark stairs relying on a single flashlight, the sound of something scraping against the metal railing echoes from upstairs.
48: On the dark stairwell, the White Spikes—white monsters that shoot spikes and climb walls—finally reveal themselves.
49: The moment Dan looks up, he locks eyes with one of the creatures hanging upside down from the ceiling.
50: Unfazed by a hail of bullets, the creatures drag his comrades away one by one while Dan even swings an axe to fight them off.
51: They barely make it out of the building, only for a horde of the creatures to swarm into the red, smoke-filled street.
52: As armored vehicles and helicopters rush into the street, fighter jets loaded with bombs approach from the sky.
53: Just as they drag the wounded into an underpass, the bombs drop.
54: When Dan opens his eyes at a base out at sea, he learns that most of the draftees who came with him never made it back.
55: Having barely survived, Charlie looks around the unfamiliar base bustling with helicopters, neither of them knowing where they even are.
56: Explaining why he never lets go of the claw around his neck, Dorian confesses that he learned about his own future on the day he was drafted.
57: Just then, the commander—the voice from the other side of the radio—calls for Dan.
58: When he hears that the commander's last name is Forester and that they share the same hometown, Dan freezes on the spot.
59: His little daughter has grown into a military commander and is now standing right in front of his eyes.
60: However, Muri remains cold, making it clear that this is no touching reunion.
61: Muri shows him a female White Spike, explaining that while the males can be killed with a toxin, the female alone survived it.
62: Inside the helicopter, Dan carefully asks how he died and what happened before that.
63: After driving the female out of a cave with fire, Muri rappels down herself, but the operation is jeopardized when the creature's tentacles knock her squad down.
64: Defying orders, Dan jumps from the helicopter and wrestles the female's tentacles with his bare hands until he finally locks her in the cage.
65: Right after the female is airlifted away, a swarm of males closes in, and as the two escape through the forest in an armored vehicle to reach the beach, Murilashes out at her father.
66: Muri fires a flare from the beach at sunset, and the two of them narrowly shake off the creatures.
67: Then Muri's true feelings burst out as she tells the story of a future Dan never knew.
68: She reveals that her parents separated when she was twelve, divorced when she was fourteen, and that her father died in a car crash when she was sixteen.
69: Hearing of a future in which he walks the exact same path as the father he hated so much, Dan is left speechless.
70: Once the female is transferred to the offshore research base, Muri stays on her feet with sedatives and begins searching for the secret behind how the creature's body neutralizes the toxin.
71: Bound in chains at the sea base, the female thrashes about relentlessly without a moment's rest.
72: Late at night, Dan brings two packs of combat rations, though the only thing on the menu is vegetable lasagna.
73: Through thousands of experiments continuing all night long, the bonding rate fluctuates up and down.
74: Every time the bonding rate goes up, the two look at each other and smile just like they used to when doing homework together in her childhood.
75: Then Muri casually asks if he knows that the Sabbath comes again tomorrow, which is the day Dan leaves the future.
76: Dorian remarks that the Colonel never gives up, adding that she must take after her father.
77: Finally, Muri reveals the real reason she brought her father to the future.
78: Hearing the exact words the two of them used to repeat together when she was little, Dan finally nods in agreement.
79: At that very moment, a massive swarm of creatures attacks the base to take back the female.
80: Filling the sea beyond the base's outer walls, the creatures do not stop even as naval mines detonate around them.
81: To get Dan and the toxin he carries to the Jumplink, Muri and her soldiers fight to clear a path.
82: As the Jumplink tower begins to glow, the creatures tear through the lower deck and swarm upward.
83: On the way past the engine room toward the helipad, the creatures climb up the iron pillars and Muri is badly wounded in an explosion.
84: Moving through the smoke-filled corridor, Muri keeps her gun raised in front to protect her father.
85: With the helipad right in front of them, flames and explosions erupt from all sides.
86: When a creature climbs over the railing and drags his daughter away, Dan holds onto her hand until the very end, even with only twenty seconds left before the jump.
87: Forced to let go of his daughter's hand at last, Dan falls alone onto the asphalt of 2022, still clutching the vial of toxin tightly in his hand.
88: Although the link to the future has been severed, young Muri is still waiting for her father back at home.
89: After visiting Charlie, who made it back alive in the hospital, Dan is greeted in the airport lobby by his tearful wife Emmy.
90: That night, Dan confesses everything to his wife, telling her that he met their grown-up daughter in the future.
91: When Dan mentions that the creatures first appeared in northern Russia in 2048 even though nobody ever saw a spaceship, Emmy asks a pointed question.
92: Realizing they had the timing wrong even as the world collapses into riots, Dan tracks Dorian down at a bar and borrows his claw.
93: Examined under a microscope, the claw reveals traces of volcanic ash not from Russia, but from somewhere around China or Korea.
94: The answer comes from Martin, the student at Dan's school who talked about nothing but volcanoes all through class.
95: The creatures did not fly in from space just now; they had been buried in a glacier for over a thousand years and woke up as the ice melted.
96: However, the government refuses to listen, saying they cannot fund a covert operation led by a high school biology teacher.
97: Needing someone with a plane, a pilot's skills, and the guts to ignore the government, Dan goes to see his father again.
98: Thus the team comes together, uniting his comrades who survived the future with his father, who raided an entire armory for them.
99: Inside the plane heading to Russia, Charlie is a bundle of nerves.
100: After sneaking across Russian airspace to reach a massive glacier, they track an unusual heat and magnetic signature on snowmobiles.
101: As the group races across the top of the glacier on snowmobiles, the needles on their instrument panels twitch erratically.
102: Blasting through the ice with explosives and descending into the crevasse below, the group discovers a massive alien spaceship sleeping inside.
103: Descending down the sheer ice fissure, they find an endless, cavernous expanse of ice unfolding before them.
104: After breaching the hull and entering the ship, they find dead aliens in the cockpit that are not White Spikes, but an entirely different species.
105: Inside the dark spaceship, rib-like pillars stretch endlessly as the group presses forward with their flashlights.
106: In the cargo hold, glowing orange pods are lined up without end, revealing that the White Spikes were the ship's cargo—perhaps a bioweapon meant to wipe out planets.
107: When they inject the sleeping creatures with the toxin brought from the future, the monsters melt away on the spot, but the noise wakes the other pods one by one.
108: Taking the detonator because he is going to die of cancer anyway, Dorian hands his claw over to Dan.
109: Up on the snowfield, the creatures ambush Dan's father and Charlie as well, and his father pulls the trigger without hesitation.
110: Deep inside the spaceship, surrounded by the creatures, Dorian sets off the bombs himself.
111: However, one creature with a red belly—a female—manages to escape.
112: Climbing up the ridge with his father, who insisted on following despite being told to stay behind, Dan tracks the female along the trail of blood on the snow.
113: When the female bursts out through the blizzard, father and son fire their guns wildly at the beast.
114: On the fog-shrouded snowfield, father and son stand back-to-back and wait for the female to strike.
115: As the female lunges, his father steps right in front of the beast to save his son, while Dan is thrown across the snowfield.
116: In that moment, gripping Dorian's claw as he confronts the female, Dan plunges the toxin into her with a single word, "Die," and the poisoned creature finally collapses.
117: With everything finally over on the snowfield, father and son lie side by side on the snow and look up at the sky.
118: While the explosion at the Russian glacier becomes worldwide news and politicians take all the credit, Dan could not care less.
119: Young Muri comes running out of the house, and right beside him is her grandfather, holding his granddaughter in his arms for the very first time.
120: This was the Amazon Prime Original movie *The Tomorrow War*, directed by Chris McKay of *The Lego Movie* and starring Chris Pratt.
121: In this story of a daughter from the future who changes her father, would you have been able to leave your daughter behind and return if you were in Dan's shoes—let us know in the comments.
